newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danisco sees sugar output meeting quota.
newsitem.headline: Danisco sees sugar output meeting quota.

text.p: Danish sugar producer and food and drinks group Danisco A/S said on Wednesday it expected overall sugar production from its plants in Denmark, Sweden and eastern Germany to be at 1995 levels or slightly higher.

If the rest of the season continued with a reasonable amount of rain and sun, sugar production would be slightly above its total European Union (EU) quota of some 920,000 tonnes for 1996 against 1995 output of about 922,000, a Danisco statement said.
The producer earlier announced the results of the season's third and last beet test carried out on September 23.
It said weather conditions had been excellent since the second test was carried out on September 2, although rains had been lacking in its entire growing area.
Danisco said sugar production in Denmark was still expected to exceed its EU quota of 425,000 tonnes compared with 1995 output of some 432,000.

Production in Sweden would be close to its EU quota for that country of 370,000 tonnes, against output of 356,000 last year, with eastern Germany more than exceeding its EU production quota of 126,000 tonnes.
Danisco's production in eastern Germany, where it has one factory, was approximately 134,000 tonnes in 1995, it said.
Danisco said its factories in Sweden and Denmark would start processing the beet harvest in the first week of October, with its German plant already in action since September 23.
Danisco, with a virtual monopoly on production in Denmark and Sweden, is Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer.
